newsitem.title: USA: US FCC chief wants open auction for digital radio.
newsitem.headline: US FCC chief wants open auction for digital radio.

text.p: The Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission Monday called for an open auction of the two available licenses to provide a nationwide radio service beamed via satellite.
"We should open that auction up to anyone," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt told a meeting of the National Association of Broadcasters.

Digital Audio Radio Services holds the promise of providing nationwide broadcast that is transmitted via satellite. The FCC must determine how to allocate the two available licenses that offer transmission throughout the country.
Hundt said the license holders should have broad flexibility to use the permits in the manner they best deem fit.
"We ought to have total flexibility be our watchword," Hundt said.

Hundt said that any broadcaster should be able to participate in the auction, either by bidding individually or through a joint venture. Hundt later told reporters he was "reasonably confidant" that other members of the FCC would agree with his call for an open auction.
